recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Jorge's Move and Free Range Childhoods", "body": "Jorge told Chance that he had moved his family from Long Island to Kentucky about three weeks earlier, drawn by his wife's midwifery training and the community around it. He praised the friendly neighbors, a trustworthy mechanic and local raw milk, and said he had not seen so many children playing together in the streets for ten or fifteen years. Chance and Gabe both responded warmly, and Chance congratulated him on the move and asked him to tell his wife to keep going with her training."}, {"title": "Kentucky, the Fool Card, and Dogman", "body": "The word epicenter sparked a bit of placenta wordplay, which led Gabe to explain his tarot map of the United States. Gabe said he had placed the Fool card in Kentucky, and he called the Mississippi River the placenta of the nation. He argued that Dogman lore in the southeastern hills and the Hellier series he binge watched reinforced that placement. Gabe also wondered aloud whether the phrase may the force be with you nodded to Charles Fort."}, {"title": "Sanchuniathon, Hades, and Greek Roots", "body": "Chance said he had been studying the Sanchuniathon, a Phoenician cosmology preserved through Eusebius and Philo of Byblos, and he called it a big game of telephone. He linked its figures Phos, Pyr and Phlox to Greek words for light and fire, and tied Phos to the New Testament phrase light of the world. Jorge said his Greek grandparents helped raise him and that Greek surfaced in nearly everything the hosts discussed. Chance added that Hades, filtered through the Roman Dis, still shaped English words like dissociative."}, {"title": "The Digamma, Musical Thirds, and Higgins", "body": "Chance asked Jorge why the Greek digamma, which carried the numerical value six, was moved to the end of the alphabet list. Jorge answered from music, saying two thirds make a chord and that a sixth inverts into a third. Chance pointed Gabe to The Prisoner, where the hero is Number Six, and the talk turned to the empty sixth seat in Plato's Symposium. Chance then read Godfrey Higgins quoting Bishop Marsh on the digamma letting deus be written Diws, plus another author who linked Zeus to the Hindu sky father Dyaus Pitar."}, {"title": "Dylan's Case Against Runic Antiquity", "body": "Dylan, who joined late after a gym session, spent much of the second half presenting inscribed artifacts he found suspicious, from Egypt's Famine Stela and the Vimose comb to the Negau helmet and a long line of Elder Futhark rune stones. His recurring argument was that most were not noticed until the 1600s or later, carried mediocre inscriptions, and would have needed priestly scribes if genuine. Dylan said he put truth ahead of any attachment to a theory, while the group floated the idea that some artifacts might be genuine but carved on later."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Get fired up tonight with friends Jorge Mesa (Third Eye Edify) and Slick Dissident, as we have an open ended hangout during tonight's solar eclipse energy.
